subtopic: Private Equity Fees and Expense Allocation
source_evidence: The adviser has a legal obligation to act in the best interests of each of the funds it manages and must allocate expenses among itself, its funds and the funds’ portfolio companies in accordance with this fiduciary duty.
answer: Private equity fund documents and agreements should explain the fees and expenses that the fund and its investors may incur. When an adviser manages several funds or works with portfolio companies, it must allocate expenses among itself, its funds, and those companies in line with its duty to act in each fund’s best interests. Investors should pay attention to which expenses are charged and how they are allocated.
